content: RBM3, also known as Putative RNA-binding protein 3, is a protein encoded by the RBM3 gene in humans. This gene belongs to the glycine-rich RNA-binding protein family and produces a protein that contains a single RNA recognition motif (RRM) domain. The expression of the RBM3 gene is upregulated in response to cold shock and conditions of low oxygen tension (hypoxia). Additionally, a pseudogene related to RBM3 is located on chromosome 1. Alternative transcriptional splice variants of this gene have been identified, which result in the production of different isoforms of the protein. RBM3 is classified as a cold-induced RNA-binding protein and plays a critical role in mRNA biogenesis. It also exhibits anti-apoptotic properties, meaning it can inhibit programmed cell death. Antibody-based profiling and transcriptomics analyses have demonstrated that RBM3 protein is expressed in all human tissues that have been studied. Confocal microscopy has revealed that the protein is predominantly localized within the nucleoplasm of cells. From a clinical perspective, RBM3 is considered a proto-oncogene, meaning it has the potential to contribute to tumor development and metastasis. It is also regarded as a potential biomarker for cancer. Notably, in colorectal cancer, high levels of RBM3 protein in tumor cells have been associated with improved patient survival, making it a favorable prognostic biomarker in this context.
